Uruguay Imposes Temporary Tariff on Imported Electric Grid Components

Uruguay’s Ministry of Economy announced last Thursday a provisional 20% tariff on imported electric grid components, including transformers and high-voltage cables, a measure that is already reshaping the landscape for the country’s Electric Utilities sector. The tariff, which took effect immediately and is slated for review in 90 days, was introduced to bolster domestic manufacturers amid what officials described as "unfair pricing practices" from overseas suppliers.

"The tariff is a necessary step to support local industry and secure Uruguay’s energy infrastructure," said Deputy Minister of Economy Martín Alvarez at a press briefing. He noted that the government will monitor its impact closely, with an eye toward adjusting the rate or scope depending on market developments.

Electric Utilities firms, such as MonteSol Energy and Río de Plata Power, have reported immediate cost increases on current procurement contracts for expansion and maintenance projects. “We’re seeing equipment prices rise by about 15% overnight,” said Laura Figueroa, procurement manager at MonteSol Energy. “This is likely to slow the rollout of grid upgrades in the short term.”

Trade analysts warn the measure could have lasting effects if extended. “Uruguay’s utilities sector is reliant on specialized imports, particularly for renewable integration,” explained Raúl Perdomo, an energy policy analyst. “Domestic suppliers can’t yet meet all technical requirements.”

The Uruguayan Association of Electric Utilities expressed cautious support for the move but called for clarity on the tariff’s duration and on government plans to facilitate local component production. The Ministry has not indicated when a final decision will be made.
